You can guarantee different things depending on how strong the grammar is.
If the grammar is finite-state

## Assistant
Yes — but the guarantee is conditional.
You cannot guarantee that “information inside the model” enters your structure just by asking the model to output scores. The model may compress, omit, hallucinate, or miscalibrate.
But you can build an information-theoretic bridge with guarantees of the form:
if the model output preserves enough mutual information with the latent variable, then the structure receives it\text{if the model output preserves enough mutual information with the latent variable, then the structure receives it}if the model output preserves enough mutual information with the latent variable, then the structure receives it
The core object is:
M→Y→SM \to Y \to SM→Y→S
where:
MMM = information latent in the model/context;
YYY = model-produced typed scores/fields;
SSS = your structured object: graph, strata, energy, partition function.
The critical theorem-shaped constraint is the data processing inequality:
M→Y→S⟹I(M;S)≤I(M;Y)M \to Y \to S \quad \Longrightarrow \quad I(M;S) \le I(M;Y)M→Y→S⟹I(M;S)≤I(M;Y)
Meaning:
Your structure cannot contain more information about the model’s latent knowledge than the emitted interface YYY contains.
So the bridge lives or dies on the design of YYY.

S=F(Y)S = F(Y)S=F(Y)

\Rightarrow
\text{information in }Sinformation in Y⇒information in S
